analyst_view.overall: Castellón are second with the best defence in the division (five conceded in 12 games) but have not played a league game since 1 November after their match with Eibar was postponed; they did win a Copa del Rey tie against Conquense. New since the last view: they lose Matías Orozco (suspended and away with his national team), Amir Saipi and Rodrigo Rêgo to international duty, so Pablo Hernández must rebuild his midfield around Diego Barri, with Álvaro Martín or Jari Vlak in Orozco's role. Valladolid have won two in a row but are without the suspended Iván Alejo (fifth yellow), the injured Latasa and Guille Bueno, and Homam and Balboa, who are with their national teams. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I still lean lower: Castellón have let in five goals in 12 league games and Valladolid are missing Latasa, Alejo, Balboa and Homam. The one change pushing the other way is that Castellón lose Orozco as the shield in front of their defence, so I would not go much lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I stay there. Castellón keep the ball (6,747 passes in 12 games by LaLiga's count, against Valladolid's 5,462 in 13) and use the width, but a Valladolid side without Alejo and Balboa is unlikely to win many at the other end.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. I lean a little higher: LaLiga's figures show Valladolid on 37 yellows and four reds against Castellón's 22 and two, and a home side chasing a possession team usually commits the fouls. Castellón's reshuffled midfield without Orozco may also have to stop more counters than usual. No referee has been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. I lean lower: LaLiga counts Valladolid at 135 shots in 13 games and Castellón 121 in 12, both near ten a game, and Valladolid are short of attackers. Castellón's game is about control, not volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: a Castellón defence that has conceded five league goals all season and a Valladolid attack missing Latasa, Alejo and Balboa. Castellón's main threat is Israel Suero, October's player of the month with six goals.
